dylan: Headline: seeing a 20-40ms tail bump on host preparse after yesterday's kernel-selector roll. Trace looks like tokenization + proto-unpack hotpath.
maya: oh no. any repro? CI/bench differences or production-only? :eyes:
dylan: repros locally with loadgen. flame shows user CPU on host token parser jumping from 8% -> 45% across nodes after selector picks 'vectorized-v2' kernel for small seqs.
nora: we pushed kernel fallback heuristics last week right? could be misclassification for sequence-length distribution.
sam: throwing logs: kvcache.evictions=0 -> 1200/s at same time? that smells like batching fallback -> smaller batches -> more KV churn.
maya: can you paste the perf sample lines? small snippet is fine.
dylan: here's the perf top snippet i grabbed (trimmed):
```
  22.4%  host_process  [kernel_vect_v2.so]  tokenize_fastpath
  17.1%  host_process  [libproto]          proto_unmarshal
   9.3%  host_process  [libc]               memcpy
   5.6%  host_process  [runtime]            kvcache_lookup
```
sam: that memcpy line + kvcache_lookup combo is classic tiny-chunk syndrome. when kernels produce smaller frames we end up more socket writes and smaller batching windows.
nora: i also pulled ingress telemetry around the spike window: http_grpc.writev_count per-connection doubled, avg write size halved from ~12k -> ~3.1k.
maya: can you paste the exact ingress call we used in loadgen? maybe it's triggering streaming-chunking behavior.
sam: repro command we use:
```
./loadgen --target-host hostA:8080 --streaming --payload-seq=rand(5,40) --qps=800
```
This forces variable seq lengths which exercised the selector.
dylan: hypothesis: kernel selector weights latency over aggregate token throughput; new vectorized-v2 kernel is great for long sequences but for short ones it increases host-side framing work and causes smaller writes, which trips batching heuristics and heats kvcache.
maya: plan: 1) gate selector to add min_seq threshold (try >=64), 2) run microbench with canary, 3) observe kvcache evictions and writev stats. anyone object?
sam: +1. Also suggest temporary increase to batching window (20ms -> 40ms) to see if batching absorbs the smaller frames.
nora: i'll instrument kvcache counters to add per-model eviction histograms and prefix hit-rate to our perf dashboards. that'll give us signal for rollback decisions.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: canary/kernel-selector-gate -> eng-runtime-canary at 2026-03-22T14:30:00Z by dylan
dylan: running canary now. local microbench results: latency median unchanged, p95 dropped 10ms, but p99 increased 18ms on nodes where selector used vectorized-v2 for seq<64.
maya: that's consistent with hypothesis. do we have a quick revert candidate if canary degrades production? rollback toggle exists on console right?
sam: yes - console rollout -> revert commit. I can stand by to flip if dashboard p99 > threshold.
nora: note for postmortem: add a test-case in kernel-selection e2e that simulates heavy variable short-seq traffic + streaming; the selector should be stable for that pattern.
dylan: agree. i'll open a follow-up PR adding: (a) min_seq gating, (b) batching-window default bump, (c) kvcache histograms. linking the perf traces and logs in bug: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-1892

maya: thanks. quick ask: can we add a tinyunit that asserts writev_count per-request > X for large-seq workloads? catches regressions early.
sam: added to my todo. bringing in a network-level test that verifies average write size thresholds.
nora: i'll put an alert on kvcache.evictions rate and writev.avg_size in the canary dashboard. if either flips strongly we rollback.
dylan: TL;DR: kernel selector misclassification caused smaller streaming frames -> more socket writes -> smaller batches -> KV churn -> p99 regression. Gate selector by seq-length and tune batching window as immediate mitigations. Postmortem test coverage to follow. :thumbsup:
